options.label: What is an AGM?
options.bodyHtml:
An Annual General Meeting (AGM), is a meeting where the company presents its financial statements to shareholders. Shareholders may review the accounts and raise questions about the company’s business and financial position.

For most private companies, the AGM is also where routine annual matters are dealt with, such as adopting the financial statements and noting or approving relevant company matters.

options.label: Is my company required to hold an AGM?
options.bodyHtml: In general, Singapore companies must hold an AGM unless they are exempt or have validly dispensed with holding AGMs. For non-listed companies, the AGM is generally due within 6 months after the company’s financial year-end.

options.label: When is a company exempt from holding an AGM?
options.bodyHtml:
A private company does not need to hold an AGM if it fulfils either of the following conditions:

1) Sends its financial statements to all members within 5 months after the financial year-end, and no member/ auditor has requested the AGM.

2) Dormant, not listed (or not a subsidiary of a listed company), and has total assets of $500,000 or less (consolidated value if it is an ultimate parent), and no member/ auditor has requested the AGM.

options.label: What does “dispense with AGM” mean?
options.bodyHtml: A private company may choose not to hold AGMs if all members pass a resolution to dispense with AGMs. After that, AGM matters may generally be dealt with by written resolutions instead

options.label: Can a sole director / sole shareholder company hold an AGM?
options.bodyHtml:
Yes. A company with only one director and one shareholder can still complete the required annual compliance process.

Depending on the company’s circumstances, this may be done by preparing the appropriate AGM documents, written resolutions, or documents to dispense with AGM where applicable.

options.label: Will the company secretary conduct the AGM for me?
options.bodyHtml:
As your corporate secretary, we can assist with preparing the relevant AGM documents, resolutions, notices, minutes, and Annual Return filing documents.

However, the AGM is ultimately a company meeting involving the company’s directors and shareholders. The directors and shareholders are responsible for reviewing and approving the relevant matters.

options.label: Are financial statements required if the company has operated for less than one year?
options.bodyHtml:
All Singapore-incorporated companies must prepare financial statements unless they fall within a specific exemption. Complete the form to assess whether you qualify for the exemption.

If your company has already reached its first financial year-end, financial statements may still be required even if the operating period was less than 12 months. For example, if the company was incorporated partway through the year and has a 31 December financial year-end, the first set of accounts may cover the period from incorporation to 31 December.

options.label: Does a dormant company still need to file an Annual Return?
options.bodyHtml:
Yes. A company must still file its Annual Return with ACRA even if it is inactive or dormant, as long as the company remains live.

However, a dormant company may qualify for exemption from preparing and filing financial statements if it meets the relevant requirements.

Please complete the form to assess if you qualify for the exemption.

label: Does the directors' statement include the directors' interests in shares or debentures?
help_text:
Section 201(16) of the Companies Act requires the company to prepare a directors' statement, which must be signed by two directors. The statement contains information specified in the Twelfth Schedule and includes details of directors' interests in shares or debentures of both the company and other corporate bodies. A class exemption order is available for certain companies.

If disclosure of directors' interests is not applicable (i.e. no directors’ interest in shares and debentures) to the company, you may select 'Yes' for the field "Does the directors' statement include the directors' interests in shares or debentures?

label: Specify business activity text
subtext:
Specifying your business activity

Indicate the primary and secondary activities of your business by choosing the most relevant Singapore Standard Industrial Classification (SSIC) code corresponding to your intended business activity.

The SSIC is the national standard developed by the Singapore Department of Statistics (DOS) to classify all registered firms into their respective industries based on their principal economic activity.

Refer to the following link for details: Singapore Department of Statistics | Singapore Standard Industrial Classification 2025
